Comuna de Puebla analiza eliminar el seguro de vivienda para contribuyentes cumplidos
mx.description: La Comuna de Puebla analiza eliminar el seguro de vivienda para las personas que cumplen con el pago del impuesto predial , debido a que ningún contribuyente ha solicitado el uso del beneficio en el transcurso del año. De acuerdo con el alcalde José Chedraui Budib , los recursos destinados al pago del seguro podrían ser ocupados a otras tareas, por lo que se llevará a cabo un análisis profundo sobre el tema. En entrevista con medios de comunicación, señaló que ningún contribuyente hizo uso del beneficio en el transcurso del año, por lo que es probable que el beneficio se elimine . “Estamos viéndolo, porque no hubo ningún reclamo y la verdad, fue una cantidad importante. Estamos viendo para ver si se quita (el seguro de vivienda) y ahorramos ese recurso”, puntualizó. Consulta: Infonavit llama a acreditados a activar seguro en caso de daños a su vivienda Cabe señalar que el contrato del seguro se asignó a la empresa Zurich , por un monto de 43 millones de pesos . El beneficio estará vigente a lo largo del año, en caso de que se cancele, la medida aplicaría a partir del 2027 . La póliza protege exclusivamente inmuebles de uso habitacional (casas-habitación) de contribuyentes cumplidos. Otorga una cobertura básica contra incendios (con un tope de hasta 100 mil pesos en contenidos y electrodomésticos) y pólizas complementarias por robo con violencia de contenidos de hasta 15 mil pesos . Te recomendamos leer: Valor de vivienda en Puebla sube 5.5%, por encima del aumento nacional de 4% La entrada Comuna de Puebla analiza eliminar el seguro de vivienda para contribuyentes cumplidos aparece primero en La Jornada de Oriente .

in.title: Govt to continue supporting initiatives to promote sports in J&K: Satish Sharma
in.description: Srinagar, Sep 18: Minister for Food, Civil Supplies & Consumer Affairs (FS&CA), Information Technology (IT), Youth Services & Sports, and Science & Technology, Satish Sharma, Friday attended the concluding league-stage match of the Khyber Cement Kashmir Super League 2026, powered by Athwas Retail and Athwas Hyundai, and reiterated the government’s commitment to providing Jammu & Kashmir’s young sporting talent with greater opportunities to compete, excel and build careers in sports. The Minister, as per an official statement, was the Chief Guest at the final league-stage fixture between Swift Strikers Rainawari FC and Sanctorum North United FC, witnessing an impressive display of football. Swift Strikers Rainawari FC registered a comprehensive 6–0 victory, thereby securing the fourth and final berth in the play-offs. With the completion of the league stage, Athwas India XI emerged as the league winners, while the successful teams now advance to the play-off stage to compete for the coveted championship title. During the event, Satish Sharma interacted with players, team officials and organisers and appreciated their efforts in creating a competitive platform for footballers from Jammu & Kashmir. He said that leagues such as the Kashmir Super League are important in providing young players with sustained match exposure and an opportunity to demonstrate their skills in a competitive environment. The Minister said that Jammu & Kashmir possesses considerable sporting talent and that the focus of the Youth Services & Sports Department is increasingly on identifying talent at the grassroots level, providing regular competitive exposure and creating pathways for promising sportspersons to progress to higher levels. He stressed that sporting development cannot be confined to infrastructure alone and must also include regular tournaments, professional coaching, quality competition, talent identification and opportunities for players to gain experience. Satish Sharma said that football enjoys a particularly strong following among the youth of Jammu & Kashmir, and tournaments of this nature can play an important role in converting that enthusiasm into structured sporting participation and competitive achievement. He appreciated the participation of local players in the league and said that giving them opportunities to compete before home crowds can contribute significantly to their confidence and development. He also underscored the importance of encouraging youngsters to take up sports as a disciplined pursuit and, wherever their talent permits, as a potential career. The Minister also acknowledged the contribution of coaches, referees, technical officials, team managements, organisers, sponsors and football supporters towards making the tournament successful. He said that a vibrant sporting ecosystem requires the collective participation of government institutions, sporting bodies, private partners, coaches, athletes and the community. Highlighting the wider objectives of the government’s sports policy, Satish Sharma said that efforts are being made to strengthen sports infrastructure and expand opportunities for young people across Jammu & Kashmir. He maintained that the emphasis should remain on grassroots development, inclusivity, competitive opportunities and systematic nurturing of sporting talent. The Minister said that major sporting competitions also provide an opportunity to promote discipline, teamwork, leadership, perseverance and healthy lifestyles among young people. He called upon youngsters to make sports an integral part of their lives and encouraged talented players to remain committed to continuous training and improvement. The Kashmir Super League has witnessed enthusiastic participation, competitive encounters and growing interest among football lovers, providing local players with an organised platform to compete and gain valuable experience. Congratulating Athwas India XI on being crowned league winners, Satish Sharma also congratulated Swift Strikers Rainawari FC on securing their play-off berth following their emphatic victory. He extended his best wishes to all the teams entering the knockout phase and expressed hope that the play-offs would produce further exciting and competitive football. The Minister reiterated that the government will continue to support initiatives that contribute to the development of sports in Jammu & Kashmir and provide young athletes with platforms where their talent can be recognized, developed and showcased.

sg.title: ‘In almost every French game, there’s theatre’: Dean Richards on bringing joie de vivre back to English rugby
sg.description: Doncaster Knights’ new director of rugby is passionate about the Champ, who Steve Borthwick should pick from overseas and getting players to have a bit of fun Turn up at Castle Park in Doncaster this week and, bang on cue, a pony and trap is being driven in stately fashion down the nearby main road. There is, some might argue, a similarly retro feel about the Knights’ latest choice of director of rugby. It is now 40 years since Dean Richards barged his way into the public consciousness with two tries on his Test debut against Ireland at Twickenham but, at 63, he is still very much up for a challenge. As with vinyl records and fine wine, old-school rugby nous never goes entirely out of vogue. That, at least, is the rationale behind Richards’ return to the upper rungs of the English club ladder, commencing with a 740-mile round trip to Cornish Pirates on the opening weekend of the 2026-27 Champ season. “If it’s ingrained in you and you love the sport, then there’s no reason why you shouldn’t continue in some capacity,” he says softly, gazing out of the window at his latest field of dreams. sg.title: We wanted to let Max Dowman bloom in the shadows but he has become hard to ignore | Barney Ronay
sg.description: This most modern and well-honed of footballers will not be able to escape the spotlight in an age of constant scrutiny but looks equipped to handle it The poet Jorge Luis Borges wrote a famous short story about a society that had become so good at making maps, so obsessed with capturing every detail, that its rulers decided the only way to do the job right was to make a lifesize map of its entire empire, which could then be laid out across the actual land from coast to coast. Imagine a map of Britain the exact same size as Britain, showing every branch of Greggs, every nail bar, every Vape shop in perfect detail. Only then can we really see what Britain looks like, by standing on a fake Britain laid over the top of actual Britain. Borges was writing in the 1940s, at a time when people were fascinated by the mechanised future, with its new forms of measuring out the world: the wireless, the 30mph motorcar, the rise of Big Tape Measure. And to be fair, the mega-map is a pretty accurate vision of our own fully networked present, a place where you can snoop around a village in Mozambique from your laptop in Egham, where no one ever stops committing acts of minute self-surveillance, even if they think they’re just searching “what is beetroot?” on the internet. ae.title: Mansoor bin Mohammed highlights UAE’s Asian Games record ahead of Aichi-Nagoya 2026
ae.description: Dubai: His Highness Sheikh Mansoor bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, President of the UAE Olympic Committee, highlighted the UAE’s growing record of achievement at the Asian Games as the country prepares for its 13th appearance at the continental sporting event. The 20th Asian Games, which open tomorrow in Japan’s Aichi Prefecture and Nagoya, run until 4 October. More than 11,000 athletes and 6,000 coaches and officials from 45 countries will take part in 16 days of competition. His Highness Sheikh Mansoor said the achievements of Emirati athletes over the years have become part of the UAE’s sporting history and continue to inspire new generations. “Our sporting achievements are a source of pride and reflect the dedication of our athletes and the support they receive from a leadership that has provided every opportunity for them to succeed and excel,” His Highness said. The UAE made its Asian Games debut in Bangkok in 1978 and has since built a medal tally of 60 across 11 sports, comprising 12 gold, 21 silver and 27 bronze medals. The UAE delegation comprises 165 athletes – 117 men and 48 women. Picture credit: GDMO The country won its first Asian Games medal at Hiroshima 1994, when Mohammed Al Qubaisi took silver in the individual bowling competition. At Doha 2006, Her Highness Sheikha Maitha bint Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum became the first Emirati woman to win an Asian Games medal, securing silver in karate. His Highness Sheikh Mansoor said these milestones helped establish the UAE as a consistent presence on Asian Games podiums and encouraged subsequent generations of athletes. More than half of the UAE’s 60 medals have been won at the last two editions of the Games, reflecting the improvement in the country’s competitive performance. He also highlighted the growth in women’s participation, with 48 female athletes competing at Aichi-Nagoya 2026, compared with 38 at Hangzhou 2022. The UAE delegation comprises 165 athletes – 117 men and 48 women – competing in athletics, swimming, taekwondo, padel, football, esports, equestrian, cycling, archery, rowing, sailing, fencing, golf, shooting, judo, modern pentathlon, triathlon, jiu-jitsu, rugby and weightlifting. The equestrian team will compete in show jumping and dressage. The UAE made its Asian Games debut in Bangkok in 1978 and has since built a medal tally of 60 across 11 sports, comprising 12 gold, 21 silver and 27 bronze medals. Picture credit: GDMO The UAE will make its Asian Games debut in modern pentathlon and padel. The rugby sevens team has been drawn alongside Sri Lanka, Singapore and the Philippines. The UAE football team has already begun its campaign, losing 3-1 to Iran in Group B, which also includes China and North Korea. Aichi-Nagoya 2026 features 43 sports and 71 disciplines, with 1,407 medals to be awarded across 469 events. It is the world’s second-largest multi-sport event after the Summer Olympic Games. The opening ceremony will be held at Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletics Stadium under the slogan ‘Imagine One Asia’. This is the third time Japan has hosted the Asian Games, following Tokyo in 1958 and Hiroshima in 1994.

ae.title: Moonshot plugs Kimi into the data feeds Wall Street already pays for
ae.description: The case Moonshot is making for Kimi in finance does not rest on benchmark scores. It rests on a roster of data vendors. On Thursday the Beijing startup said investment banks, funds and venture capital firms are already running its Kimi models inside AI tools, and it put names to the claim: investment bank CICC, plus venture capital firms including Sequoia China, now rebranded as Hong Shan. The disclosure landed alongside the launch of Kimi for financial services. That is the detail worth watching. Not the model. The wiring. The partner roster is the product According to Moonshot, Kimi users can pull the information typically used for analysis and reports directly, by way of industry data partners that include S&P Global Market Intelligence, Crunchbase, Wind, local financial news leaders and business database Tianyancha. Kimi can also reach into the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission's EDGAR system for public companies' financial filings, the startup said, along with the IMF, the World Bank and the Federal Reserve Economic Data site, better known as FRED. Three of those are free public sources that anyone can query without paying for an AI subscription. It is the paid vendors that are the interesting half, because getting S&P Global and Wind data licensed into a consumer-facing chat product is a contract problem rather than an engineering one. What a look at the mobile app revealed Nothing separate has to be downloaded. Testing on Kimi's mobile app indicated that the kinds of data on offer varied from user to user depending on subscription tier. Data access, in other words, is gated, and the gate is whichever plan you hold. Subscriptions open at 49 yuan ($7.31) a month and climb to 699 yuan ($104.23). That makes the top tier roughly 14 times the price of the entry one, and Moonshot has not said where on that ladder the vendor feeds sit. To put $104.23 a month in perspective against what else it might buy: this is not a Bloomberg terminal seat. Then again, it makes no claim to be one. A Deutsche Bank manager turns up in the promo video A promotional video Moonshot put out Thursday features Samuel Fischer, Beijing branch manager at Deutsche Bank. "The real inflection point really is the combination of stronger AI capabilities with professional expertise," Fischer said. "AI companies that understand real financial workflows and can deliver reliability and data security will be particularly well positioned to contribute to this transformation." He added: "AI can now organize and compare this kind of information, identify inconsistencies, and support initial analysis." Take a close look at that second quote. Organize, compare, flag inconsistencies, support initial analysis. Each of those verbs belongs to an assistant. Not one of them is a decision. Whether Deutsche Bank is a client was not immediately clear. The bank declined to comment. A branch manager turning up in a vendor's launch video does not amount to a procurement contract, and that silence is carrying some weight here. The IPO question sitting behind all of it Reports say Moonshot has filed confidentially for a Hong Kong IPO. The company said it does not comment on market rumors or speculation. A roster of named clients and a wall of licensed data partners happens to be precisely the sort of material that renders a revenue story legible to bankers. Nobody at Moonshot is saying whether that timing is coincidental. The model underneath it Kimi K3, which arrived in July, competes with models from leading U.S. companies. That is the backdrop rather than the story. The story is that a Chinese AI company has concluded the route into finance is not a cleverer model. It is demonstrating that an analyst can be handed a Tianyancha record and an EDGAR filing in a single reply without ever opening a second tab. Anyone sizing this up should not be asking Moonshot how Kimi reasons. The question is which of those data partners comes with the 49 yuan tier, and which one runs you 699.

sa.title: زين الدين زيدان يعلق على إمكانية ضم كريم بنزيما لـ منتخب فرنسا.. ماذا قال؟
sa.description:
علق زين الدين زيدان المدير الفني لمنتخب فرنسا، عن إمكانية ضم كريم بنزيما لاعب الهلال السابق لقائمة المنتخب خلال الفترة المقبلة بصورة رسمية، في ظل الرغبة في حسم هذا الملف.

وقال زين الدين زيدان في تصريحات إعلامية:" أنا أعشق كريم بنزيما، لقد لعب سابقاً مع المنتخب، وهو الآن في سن معينة، ومثل (كانتي) أنا معجب جداً بمسيرته الكروية. الان أحتاج إلى رؤية لاعبين أصغر سناً بعض الشيء لكي نرى ما يمكننا فعله معاً".

وكان زين الدين زيدان، قد تولي تدريب منتخب فرنسا خلال الفترة الماضية، وذلك خلفا لديشامب، وذلك بعد فشل الأخير في تحقيق لقب كأس العالم 2026، والتي أقيمت في الولايات المتحدة الأمريكية وكندا والمكسيك.

وفسخ نادي الهلال، عقده مع كريم بنزيما من طرف واحد خلال الفترة الماضية، وذلك بقرار فني من جانب سيميوني إنزاغي المدير الفني للفريق، لعدم الحاجة لجهوده.

ml.title: PMU-Mali: Programme officiel du dimanche 20 septembre 2026
Campagne agricole : Les engrais restent difficiles d’accès
ml.description: © Internet Pluies irrégulières et difficultés d’accès aux engrais pèsent sur la campagne agricole 2026 - 2027. Localement, l’espoir repose sur la contre-saison. Dotée d’un budget de 164,39 milliards de francs CFA, la campagne vise 11,92 millions de tonnes de céréales. Fin mars, les stocks d’engrais couvraient seulement 22% des besoins estimés, selon la FAO. Dans les zones habituellement arrosées, le manque de pluies inquiète. « Cette année, la principale difficulté reste celle de l’eau. L’an passé, au mois d’août, nous avions enregistré environ 300 mm de pluie, contre seulement 100 mm à la même période cette année », témoigne Seydou Coulibaly, paysan à Wakoro, près de Dioïla. En visite dans la région les 5 et 6 septembre, le ministre de l’Agriculture a fait état d’un taux de réalisation de 80% des superficies. Il a lié la réussite de la campagne à la poursuite des pluies jusqu’en octobre. La zone est stratégique pour le coton, le maïs et le mil. Malgré l’aspect satisfaisant des cotonniers, le retard des engrais a conduit à reconvertir 12 123 hectares de coton en mil, selon la direction locale de la CMDT à Fana. Les producteurs espèrent encore sauver le mil, beaucoup moins le maïs. Circuit de distribution inefficace Plus que la faiblesse des pluies, l’entretien du réseau irrigué et l’accès aux engrais ont entravé les activités à Niono, principal bassin rizicole du pays, où intervient l’Office du Niger. « La pluie n’a pas été abondante, mais c’est surtout l’entretien du réseau qui a posé problème. Dans l’ensemble, le riz présente un bon aspect. À présent, nous avons un problème d’engrais », explique Bréhima Cissouma, membre d’une coopérative de 100 producteurs à Niono. Pour obtenir l’engrais subventionné, les paysans doivent présenter une caution délivrée au terme d’une procédure contraignante. Le sac de 50 kg d’engrais minéraux coûte 15 000 francs CFA au tarif subventionné, contre 30 000 francs CFA hors subvention, selon les producteurs interrogés. « Nous n’avons pas pu obtenir les cautions avant la date limite du 15 août pour avoir l’engrais organique », précise M. Cissouma. Les signatures demandées auprès de la Chambre d’Agriculture, de la Filière Riz et du Contrôle financier allongent une procédure pourtant soumise au calendrier agricole. Dans cette zone irriguée, l’espoir repose encore sur la contre-saison, si les engrais disponibles sont remis à temps.

ml.title: UFOA-A U17 : Le Mali tombe avant le dernier carré
ml.description: © Internet Le tournoi de l’UFOA-A U17 2026 entre dans sa phase décisive au Sénégal. La Gambie, la Guinée, le Liberia et le Sénégal ont rejoint le dernier carré, tandis que le Mali quitte prématurément la compétition et manquera la prochaine CAN U17. Lancée le 7 septembre, la compétition a rapidement dégagé une hiérarchie dans le groupe A. Pays hôte et double tenant du titre zonal, le Sénégal a dominé la Mauritanie (4-0), puis surclassé la Sierra Leone (5-0), avant de boucler la phase de groupes par un nul face à la Gambie (0-0). Avec sept points, les Lionceaux terminent premiers, devant les Baby Scorpions, également solides, vainqueurs de la Sierra Leone (4-1) et de la Mauritanie (3-1). Dans le groupe B, la disqualification de la Guinée-Bissau après les tests IRM a réduit la poule à trois équipes. Le Liberia en a pris les commandes avec un nul contre le Mali (1-1), puis une victoire face à la Guinée (2-1), synonyme de qualification. Le coup d’arrêt des Aiglonnets Finaliste de la précédente édition à domicile, le Mali n’aura jamais réellement lancé son tournoi. Face au Liberia, les Aiglonnets ont dû attendre la 89 ème minute pour arracher le match nul face à un adversaire que leurs aînés avaient écrasé 6-0 à l’ouverture du tournoi en 2025. Ce point les plaçait pourtant en position favorable avant le duel décisif contre la Guinée : un nul suffisait pour atteindre les demi-finales. Le Mali a même frappé le premier en ouvrant le score dès la 2 ème minute, grâce à Adama Keïta. Mais le Syli Cadet a égalisé avant la pause, puis renversé la rencontre en seconde période pour s’imposer finalement 2-1. Deux matches, un seul point et une élimination dès la phase de groupes : le bilan est sévère pour une sélection habituée aux premiers rôles continentaux. Les Aiglonnets manqueront ainsi la prochaine CAN U17, une première depuis 2019, si l’on excepte l’édition 2021, annulée. Le tournoi se poursuit ce jeudi 17 septembre au stade Lat-Dior de Thiès, avec deux demi-finales au programme. Le Sénégal sera opposé à la Guinée, tandis que la Gambie en découdra avec le Liberia. Au-delà d’une place en finale, l’enjeu sera continental, puisque les deux finalistes décrocheront leur qualification pour la prochaine CAN U17. La finale est programmée le 20 septembre. Mohamed Kenouvi

zw.title: Legal showdown looms as developer rejects Beitbridge council contract termination
zw.description: Thupeyo Muleya, Beitbridge Bureau A LEGAL showdown is looming between the Municipality of Beitbridge and land developer Kingdom Lifestyle Africa (Private) Limited after the company rejected the local authority’s decision to terminate its contract for the development of Matibe (Eastlea) low-density residential stands. The municipality earlier this week announced the termination of its Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with Kingdom Lifestyle Africa and directed beneficiaries of the Eastlea project to redirect all payments to the council. The decision was contained in Public Notice No. 38/2026 dated September 13, 2026. However, Kingdom Lifestyle Africa has disputed the termination, arguing that the municipality had no legal basis to cancel the agreement and had failed to follow due process. In a statement issued on Thursday, the developer said it regarded the purported termination as unlawful and insisted that the MOU remained valid and binding. “The purported termination by the Municipality is disputed and unlawful; the Municipality has no lawful basis to terminate the Memorandum of Understanding, nor do they have the right to arbitrarily terminate a binding contract like they purport to have done,” said the company. Kingdom Lifestyle Africa said the termination was substantively and procedurally defective, adding that its contractors and personnel remained on site and that construction work at the Eastlea development was continuing. The company also moved to reassure beneficiaries affected by the conflicting directives, telling them to contact its offices for clarification on their stands and accounts. “For the avoidance of doubt, beneficiaries are advised to continue making all payments, instalments and any other obligations relating to their Eastlea stands directly to Kingdom Lifestyle (Africa) private limited, through the same channels and accounts previously used,” said the developer. It said it would continue recognising receipts, records and account statements issued to beneficiaries and would ensure that payments were accounted for and applied towards the respective stands. Kingdom Lifestyle Africa warned beneficiaries against redirecting payments to other parties, saying they would do so at their own risk and that the company would not accept responsibility for any loss, double payment or dispute over ownership or account status arising from such action. “Kingdom Lifestyle (Africa) Ltd is not forcing a relationship here but is bound by a live contract. If the Municipality is serious about terminating the said contract, they should do so the right and legal way, respecting the interests of all stakeholders involved,” reads the statement. The developer said the municipality’s position risked creating confusion around the project and affecting beneficiaries who were not party to the dispute. Despite the standoff, Kingdom Lifestyle Africa said it remained committed to the Eastlea project and was open to constructive engagement with the municipality to resolve the matter amicably and in the best interests of beneficiaries.
